# Capability map

Generated by `python -m ctf engines generate` from the engine manifests (`<module>.manifest.toml`)
and the first sentence of each engine's docstring. Do not edit by hand:
`tests/test_engines_capabilities.py` fails when this file is stale. After a merge that touches
engines, regenerate it instead of resolving conflicts line by line.

This is what `python -m ctf triage` (ctf/triage.py) can suggest, and when. Triage lists every engine
whose route matches the challenge, best priority first: routes that name a category apply only
there, keyword routes need a word of the description, file routes need a downloaded file.

- **class**: `executes` (a CLI that scans its output for flags), `analysis` (a CLI that reports
  facts), `plan` (builds candidates, never runs them), `library` (import-only: call it from Python;
  `ctf run` refuses it).
- **priority**: the route's priority (0-100, higher is listed first).
- **when**: `always` = suggested for every challenge of that category; otherwise the keywords
  (lower-case substrings of the description) or the file matchers (`ext:`, `magic:`, `name:`).
- Per-engine detail (status, cost, needs, tests) is in [coverage/ENGINES.md](coverage/ENGINES.md);
  the hand-written map carried from CSCTF 2026 is kept, unmaintained, in
  [capabilities-carried.md](capabilities-carried.md).

## Binary toolbox

Host tools no engine ships, which past editions needed to solve a challenge. Listed in
`tools/toolbox.toml`; `python -m ctf toolbox verify` checks them (the preflight doctor
runs it as check `toolbox`), `python -m ctf toolbox install` plans or runs the installs.

| tool | role | what it gives | past need | install | playbook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sops` | core | decrypt a sops-encrypted YAML/JSON/ENV file with a leaked age/PGP key | key-leak to decrypt chains (2024/2025 opsec archetype) | brew `sops` | [opsec](playbooks/opsec.md) |
| `age` | core | decrypt an age file with a leaked identity; age-keygen derives the recipient | 2025 Parano1d (ccrypt, then KeePass, then age) | brew `age` | [opsec](playbooks/opsec.md) |
| `rclone` | core | reveal an obscured rclone.conf password; read a crypt remote with a leaked config | key-leak to decrypt chains (rclone config archetype) | brew `rclone` | [opsec](playbooks/opsec.md) |
| `git-crypt` | core | unlock a git-crypt repository with a leaked symmetric key | 2025 Secret (git-crypt history) | brew `git-crypt` | [opsec](playbooks/opsec.md) |
| `ccrypt` | core | decrypt a .cpt file with a leaked passphrase | 2025 Parano1d (ccrypt, then KeePass, then age) | brew `ccrypt` | [opsec](playbooks/opsec.md) |
| `websocat` | core | talk to a WebSocket endpoint from the shell (client, listener, relay) | 2025 rev Covert: a second localhost websocket listener | brew `websocat` | [web](playbooks/web.md) |
| `keepassxc-cli` | core | open a KeePass .kdbx with a leaked password or key file (show, export); never a cracker | 2025 Parano1d and Acme Analytics chains | cask `keepassxc` | [opsec](playbooks/opsec.md) |
| `macfuse` | core | the FUSE layer VeraCrypt mounts volumes through on macOS | needed by veracrypt | cask `macfuse` |  |
| `veracrypt` | core | open a VeraCrypt/TrueCrypt volume in text mode (outer or hidden decoy volume) with a leaked password | 2025 Parano1d decoy volume | cask `veracrypt` (needs `macfuse`) | [forensics](playbooks/forensics.md) |
| `nss` | core | Mozilla NSS (libnss3), which firefox_decrypt loads to decrypt logins.json | needed by firefox_decrypt | brew `nss` |  |
| `firefox_decrypt` | core | decrypt the saved logins of a Firefox profile folder (key4.db + logins.json, primary password if set) | 2025 forensics Artifacts: Firefox profile, then the vault password, then 7z | pinned clone (needs `nss`) | [forensics](playbooks/forensics.md) |
| `sage` | optional | SageMath for lattice, isogeny and number-field crypto | lattice and isogeny crypto (several editions) | manual | [crypto](playbooks/crypto.md) |
